cues.text: Replay the bad news principle. When you can wait, it is mainly the bad possible outcomes that decide whether you build now.
So the question to ask is: what does this policy actually compress?
In financial markets, there is a price for carrying risk. Quantitative easing pushes that price down. Squeeze the spring.
But the doubt inside a firm is a different thing. Will anyone still be buying in three years? Will this factory still make sense?
Those are different worries entirely. A central bank buying government bonds reaches them only indirectly, if at all.
So the honest version of his claim is about how directly, not about whether.
What a central bank reaches directly is the price at which risk trades.
What it reaches at one or two removes is the doubt itself.
